summary_markdown:
## Behavior changes
1. (user_visible, needs_operator) Wording: when the desktop cut a Run output and keryx has to cut again, the stored note (and the replayed card) reads `[… earlier output was cut; the end of the output follows]`, then `[… N more bytes cut here]`, then the tail. Before, the desktop's line was cut away and `[… N earlier bytes not kept]` stood alone. Outputs without the desktop's line keep the old marker. Alternative: `[… keryx dropped N more bytes here]`.
2. (user_visible, decided) `detectSecrets`, shared by every redaction consumer: an `-----END … PRIVATE KEY-----` with no header before it now masks only the key body above it: base64 lines (also with a cat -n, grep/rg -n or ctx rg line-number prefix, or indented), PEM header fields, and the blank lines between them. On the END's own line it masks the run of base64 and `\n`/`\r` escapes, which stops at a quote. Before, it masked back to the previous block or the start of the input. Fails open for a key tail laid out in a way this does not recognise (for example `> ` quoted lines or a space-joined body): then only the END marker and its same-line base64 run are masked.
3. (model-facing, decided) A compaction summary's Run-results section lists `- [terminal run <id> result: <outcome>]` only, without the command. Items carried from an older summary lose their command text too.
4. (model-facing, decided; reaches non-Run sessions too) In-turn compaction counts the Run-result head against the tail. Its share is the budget minus the messages after it, which take at most half. Over its share, keryx's line and the newest notes that fit are kept and the older notes are only named. `compactWithFallback` now checks `fits` on the in-turn cut. When the cut does not fit, it halves the tail, down to 1,000 tokens, and takes the largest tail that fits, or the smallest one tried when none fits. When `fits([])` is false (the overflow retry with no known limit), it keeps the full-tail cut as before. This applies to every in-turn cut, not only to Run results.
5. (wire, shared with T14) A terminal-results prompt whose every run id already has a stored note gets `{stopReason: "end_turn", _meta: {keryx: {terminalResults: {stored: 0, duplicates: [...]}}}}`: nothing is stored, no turn runs and no model call is made. With some new entries, only those are stored and the turn runs; that answer carries no extra meta. Duplicates are found in the live history and the archive, so a note that compaction removed still counts.
6. (user_visible) The Telegram/Hub history restore now shows the agent reply that proposed a Run (the continuation line ends the turn and is not an item).

## For the orchestrator / docs lane
- The spec should name the all-duplicate answer, the head-only Run-results items and the head budget rule (metrics.doc_deltas).
- `TERMINAL_OUTPUT_CUT_LINE` (src/acp/terminal-result.ts) equals the desktop's `RUN_OUTPUT_CUT` today. Nothing pins the two together yet: the desktop drift test could (T14 lane).

acceptance.criterion: R2-SC-003 decision 1: an orphan END masks the key body directly above it. A cut key in Run output keeps the line above its body (the desktop's cut line), a peer-agent frame above an orphan END survives, a JSON document holding an orphan END in a string value still parses after redaction, and the text before a lone END line in a test file is not masked. The scan stays linear.
acceptance.evidence: secrets.test.ts: 9 new orphan-END cases. All 9 were red with the old span `[from, stop]` and are green now. terminal-result.test.ts 'R2-SC-003: a key cut by the desktop's tail…' is red→green the same way. Linear-time tests: 8000 orphan ENDs and 20,000 body+END blocks, both green. `ctx rg --all -n "END [A-Z0-9 ]{0,40}PRIVATE KEY" src/security/detect/secrets.test.ts` now lists 26 of 28 lines. Before, it listed 5 of 7 lines of the old file.

acceptance.criterion: R2-HL3-001 decision 2: the pinned head counts against the budget; over its share it keeps the newest notes that fit (always the continuation line) and names the rest; the in-turn cut respects `fits`. Test: 8 near-maximum notes on a small window give a request that fits.
acceptance.evidence: compact-fallback.test.ts 'R2-HL3-001: eight near-maximum results…' (default tail, fits < 16K tokens) and 'R2-HL3-001: the head counts against the tail…' are red against HEAD's compact.ts. They also fail under the mutants share=∞ (both), no fits search (the first) and no reserve for the rounds after the head (the second).

acceptance.criterion: R2-SC-002 decision 3: the summary keeps only keryx's validated head line per removed note, never the client-supplied command text.
acceptance.evidence: compact-fallback.test.ts 'R2-SC-002: the summary names a removed Run by keryx's head line only…' (an instruction-shaped command) and 'R2-SC-002: an earlier summary that carried a command keeps only the head line…' are red against HEAD and green now.

acceptance.criterion: R2-AR-003 decision 4: the note grammar lives in src/session/terminal-note.ts, used by src/acp/terminal-result.ts and src/session/compact.ts; the compaction tests build their notes with the producer.
acceptance.evidence: terminal-note.ts holds the run-id pattern, head-line builder and reader, the outcome words, the command/duration/output/tag prefixes and storedTerminalNoteHead. terminal-result.ts builds and parses the note from it: NOTE_HEAD is gone and the parser reads line by line. compact.ts no longer has its own RUN_RESULT_HEAD. compact-fallback.test.ts builds its notes with parseTerminalResults + terminalResultNote. terminal-note.test.ts adds 9 tests. The producer/parser tests (57) pass unchanged in substance.

acceptance.criterion: R2-DG-004 decision 5: a terminalContinuation user line closes the turn in qualifyingHistory without adding an item.
acceptance.evidence: topic-history.test.ts 'keryx's continuation line closes the turn before it…' is red against HEAD's history.ts and green now.

acceptance.criterion: R2-LG-004 decision 6: keryx's tail cut keeps the desktop's leading cut line first; its marker says only how many further bytes keryx dropped. Test with output that grows under redaction.
acceptance.evidence: terminal-result.test.ts 'R2-LG-004: the desktop's cut line stays first…' uses a 16 KiB request log full of 127.0.0.1. It is red under the plain tail-cut mutant (HEAD's code) and green now. 'R2-LG-004: a desktop tail under the cap keeps its cut line and gets no keryx marker' is green.

acceptance.criterion: R2-HL-002 decision 7 (server half): skip entries whose runId already has a stored note; store only new ones; an all-duplicate prompt stores nothing, starts no turn, makes no model call and answers end_turn with _meta.keryx.terminalResults {stored: 0, duplicates}. Tests for all three cases.
acceptance.evidence: terminal-result.server.test.ts 'R2-HL-002' covers three cases: mixed, all duplicates, and after session/load with one note only in the archive. All 3 are red with the dedupe removed. The load case is also red when only the history is scanned. T14's fixture answers with the same shape (apps/desktop/src/test/terminal-run-delivery.fixture.tsx:506).

acceptance.evidence: terminal-result.server.test.ts 'R2-HL-003…' expects -32600 with condition shutting-down and no stored notes. It is red when the append is moved between refuseIfBusy and refuseIfStopping.

acceptance.evidence: src/acp/profile.ts doc comment reworded (no test: comment only).

TP-002: agent-lifecycle-hooks 'R2-TP-002…' is red when `options.origin === "terminal-results"` is deleted at agent.ts:3511. TP-005: 'a head of several notes…' is red under M54 (marker) and M53 (while→if); 'a tail walk that reaches the head…' is red under M55 (no jump); M56 (keptHead) turns 8 tests red. TP-006: outcomes, newest 24 and the carried section checked with toEqual, all red at HEAD; the 200-character command clip became the SC-002 tests, since commands are no longer listed. questions.question: R2-SC-003's mirror site, an unclosed BEGIN, still masks to the end of the input (or to the next END anywhere after it). Bound it forward over the key body the same way?
questions.why: Decision 1 covered the orphan END only. The BEGIN-side span cannot strip a frame, but it still merges records: ctx rg over secrets.test.ts lists 26 of 28 lines because one record's BEGIN pairs with a later record's END, and JSON after an unclosed BEGIN still breaks. Bounding it risks a key whose body is not line-shaped (space-joined) after a cut header. The current test 'an unterminated header (head -20 id_rsa) fails closed to the end of the input' pins today's rule.

options.label: Keep the BEGIN side failing closed to the end of the input
Bound the BEGIN side forward over body lines too, in a separate change with its own tests

questions.question: When the desktop already cut an output and keryx cuts again, the marker under the desktop's line reads `[… N more bytes cut here]`. Keep this wording?
questions.why: User-visible text on the replayed run card. Decision 6 fixed the meaning (only keryx's own count, no total) but not the words.

options.label: Keep `[… N more bytes cut here]`
Use `[… keryx dropped N more bytes here]`
